This section shows how to do [Exercise 3](../exercise3.qmd) using `git` via the command-line interface (CLI). See the linked exercise for the narrative. Steps done on github.com are the same as in the linked exercise and are not repeated here.

### Forking in practice

1. Fork your partner's repository on GitHub, as shown in [Exercise 3](../exercise3.qmd#forking-in-practice). You should end up on your fork, whose URL is something like `https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/THEIR_REPO_NAME`.

1. On your fork's page, click the green `<> Code` button, select the "HTTPS" tab, and copy the URL. It should be something like `https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/THEIR_REPO_NAME.git`. In your terminal, `cd` to the folder where you want to store your fork, then clone it:

   ```bash
   git clone REPO_URL
   ```

   where `REPO_URL` is the URL you copied.

1. `cd` into the folder you just cloned and run:

   ```bash
   git remote -v
   ```

   Note that `origin` is *your fork* on GitHub, *not your partner's repository*.

1. Create a branch called `dev2` and switch to it:

   ```bash
   git checkout -b dev2
   ```

1. Use your text editor to add the following lines to `mymath.R`:

   ```r

   multiply <- function(a, b) {
      return (a*b)
   }
   ```

   Then stage and commit the change:

   ```bash
   git add -u
   git commit -m "add multiplication function to mymath file"
   ```

1. `dev2` only exists on your computer. Push it to *your fork* on GitHub:

   ```bash
   git push -u origin dev2
   ```

   Since `dev2` doesn't exist on your fork yet, `-u origin dev2` tells `git` to create it there and to make your local `dev2` track it.

1. On GitHub, open a pull request from your fork's `dev2` to your partner's `main`, and have your partner merge it, as shown in [Exercise 3](../exercise3.qmd#forking-in-practice).

   Congratulations! You and your partner have now collaborated on a new feature.

1. Sync your fork on GitHub with the "Sync fork" button, as shown in [Exercise 3](../exercise3.qmd#forking-in-practice). Then update your local `main`:

   ```bash
   git checkout main
   git pull
   ```

   ::: {.callout-tip title="Syncing from the command line" collapse="true"}
   Instead of using the "Sync fork" button, you can register your partner's repository as a second remote, conventionally called `upstream`, pull its changes, and push them to your fork:

   ```bash
   git remote add upstream https://github.com/THEIR_USERNAME/THEIR_REPO_NAME.git
   git checkout main
   git pull upstream main
   git push
   ```

   You only need to add `upstream` once.
   :::

1. Now that your changes are merged into your partner's `main` and your fork is synced, delete your development branch:

   ```bash
   git branch -d dev2
   ```
